title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share
summary: Anthropic set the price of its first public shares at $83, higher than the $70 to $78 range it gave earlier. It sold more shares than first planned and raised about $81.3 billion, more than any listing before it. The stock is set to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.
why: When a company prices its shares above the planned range, it usually means a lot of investors wanted in. How the stock does on its first days can affect other AI stocks, including companies that own part of Anthropic, like Amazon and Alphabet.

title: Big tech names join Anthropic's private share sale
summary: Besides the public offering, Anthropic is selling about $26 billion of stock in a private sale at the same $83 price. Alphabet's Google, Microsoft and AMD are among the buyers. Counting both parts, the total raised comes to about $107.3 billion.
why: When big companies put money into a partner, their fortunes become more linked. If Anthropic does well, these investors could benefit; if it struggles, it could weigh on them a little too.

title: Walmart reports results before the market opens
summary: Walmart, one of the largest retailers in the United States, shares its quarterly results this morning before trading starts. Its shares slipped a little in early trading ahead of the report. Investors will look closely at sales and at what the company expects for the holiday season.
why: Walmart sells to millions of families, so its results act like a check-up on how much people are spending. That can move the whole market, not just Walmart.
